title: The Negotiation Workbook
h1: Stop Talking About It. Start a D/s Dynamic That Actually Works.
subhead: An 8-section fill-in workbook that takes you from 'we've been thinking about trying this' to a real, agreed-upon D/s structure in one sitting.
tagline: An 8-section fill-in workbook. From 'we've been thinking about this' to a real D/s structure in one sitting.
meta_description: The D/s negotiation workbook. 8 sections covering desires, limits, dynamic structure, protocols, and a D/s agreement template. Start your dynamic properly.
problem:
You've had the conversation. Or the beginning of it. One of you said 'I've been thinking about something,' there was a long pause, and then somehow you ended up talking about your plans for the weekend instead. Or you started something without a framework and three weeks in, nobody's sure what the rules are, what's expected, what's okay.

The hard part isn't wanting this. The hard part is the transition from 'we want it' to 'here's what it actually looks like.'

That transition needs a structure. This is that structure.
inside: Section 1: What we each want — guided prompts for both partners to articulate desires, fears, and expectations clearly
Section 2: Activity map — a structured way to work through what's on the table, what's not, and what's a 'maybe with more conversation'
Section 3: Dynamic structure — define what your D/s actually looks like day-to-day vs. scene-specific
Section 4: Limits — hard, soft, and the nuanced middle. A framework that goes beyond the simple 'what are your hard limits' question
Section 5: Protocols and rituals — the small structures that make the dynamic feel real outside of scenes
Section 6: D/s agreement template — a complete, fill-in document that formalizes what you've agreed to
Section 7: 30-day review guide — structured questions for a check-in after your first month
Section 8: 90-day review guide — how the dynamic evolves over time, what to renegotiate
who_for: You've been wanting to start a D/s dynamic and the conversation keeps not quite happening
You started something but it feels informal and undefined — like you're making it up as you go
You want a documented framework you can both reference, adjust, and come back to
who_not: This is a workbook — it requires both partners to participate. If only one of you is bought in, this will sit in a drawer
If you're looking for inspiration or education about what D/s is — this assumes you already know. It's the how to start it, not what is it

faq.q: Do we fill this in together or separately?
faq.a: Both. Some sections are designed to be answered separately first (so you're not influencing each other), then compared and discussed together. The workbook walks you through which is which.

faq.q: What if we disagree on things when we fill it in?
faq.a: That's the point. The workbook is designed to surface the disagreements in a structured setting — with prompts to work through them — rather than have them emerge mid-scene when there's no framework to resolve them.
For most couples, 60-90 minutes in a single sitting. Some sections prompt longer conversations. The 30 and 90-day reviews take about 20 minutes each.
